changes.proposed_value: Do not call this the first human discovery; local prior knowledge is not erased, and Fawcett wrote that residents had known the cave for at least 12 or 15 years. Sources disagree on the year: 1894 (S012; Ajit Kumar 2013), 1895 (S011 and the state tourism page), and about the beginning of 1896 (a report quoted in Fawcett 1901, p. 412). The 1894–1896 interval bounds the conflicting reports; it does not assert visits in every intervening year.

changes.proposed_value: The research institution supports the second-century date of the Geography. Geography 7.1.8 (Mouziris, an emporium) and 7.1.86 (Karoura, royal seat of Kerobothros) were inspected in OCR of McCrindle’s 1885 English translation and commentary. These remain attributed identifications; original Greek, scan images and a modern critical edition were not verified. Ptolemy’s coordinates are not modern positions.
